theorem.statement: If every cost and driver layer is a tensor product over a variable partition, the layered unitary factorises over that partition for any input; if the initial state is also a product across the partition, so does the output state.
theorem.operator_statement: Block-local layers imply U = tensor_product_i U_i independently of the input state.
theorem.state_corollary: A block-product input remains a block-product output; states may be internally entangled within each block.
theorem.set_cover_support_partition: connected components of the primal graph joining variables that occur in a common cost term
theorem.geometric_sufficient_relation: for radius-R metric coverage, E(G_ZZ) is a subset of E(G_base(2R))
limitations: cross-block entanglement prevents product-state factorisation but not operator factorisation
a mixer or preparation gate crossing the partition merges circuit blocks
low treewidth is a weaker simulation route than exact block factorisation

random_incidence_hypergraphs.qualification: For the set-cover squared penalty this follows by construction: every cost hyperedge becomes a clique in the primal interaction graph.

sparse_connected_path.lesson: sparsity alone does not imply exact block factorisation

dense_disconnected_cliques.lesson: geometry is not necessary for exact block factorisation

one_dimensional_geometric_path.lesson: geometric locality may give low width without giving disconnected blocks

nonproduct_initial_state.example: (|01>+|10>)/sqrt(2) across two otherwise independent one-qubit blocks
nonproduct_initial_state.lesson: block-local unitaries preserve this entanglement; they do not turn the state into a product

bridging_driver.example: exp(-i beta X_i X_j) with i and j in different cost blocks
bridging_driver.lesson: a mixer edge merges the circuit support blocks even when the cost Hamiltonian is disconnected
